subject: Climate & Environment
title: Typhoons and Cyclones Around the World
description: One-minute skill: Typhoons and Cyclones Around the World.

hook.text: Hurricanes, typhoons, and cyclones are all the same storm. The name depends on where it forms.

buildup.text: Atlantic storms are hurricanes. Pacific storms are typhoons. Indian Ocean storms are cyclones.

discovery.text: The western Pacific produces the most and the strongest tropical storms on Earth each year.

twist.text: Typhoon Haiyan in 2013 hit the Philippines with 315 km/h winds — one of the strongest ever recorded.

climax.text: Bangladesh has lost over 500,000 people to cyclones since 1970. Geography makes it vulnerable.

punchline.text: Same storm, different name. The destruction doesn't change with the label.

quiz.question: What determines whether a storm is called a hurricane, typhoon, or cyclone?
options: The ocean basin where it forms

details.summary: Hurricanes, typhoons, and cyclones are the same weather phenomenon given different names by region. Typhoons in the western Pacific are the most frequent and among the most intense, while cyclones strike South and Southeast Asia, Australia, and the Indian Ocean.
details.whyItMatters: Tropical cyclones are the costliest weather disasters globally and affect the most vulnerable tropical populations. Regional differences in intensity and preparedness shape their human toll.
takeaways: The western Pacific produces the most tropical cyclones of any basin
Typhoon Haiyan hit the Philippines in 2013 with 315 km/h winds
Bangladeshi cyclones have historically killed hundreds of thousands

faq.question: Why does the western Pacific produce the strongest storms?
faq.answer: The western Pacific has the largest area of warm water above 26 degrees Celsius and favorable atmospheric conditions year-round. Super typhoons can intensify over long ocean fetches without encountering land or cool water to weaken them.

faq.question: How has Bangladesh reduced cyclone deaths?
faq.answer: Bangladesh built thousands of concrete cyclone shelters, established community early-warning volunteer networks, and improved evacuation planning. Cyclone deaths have dropped from hundreds of thousands in 1970 to a few thousand in recent major storms.
